wu: Students play 'Speed Review' in teams of 4. Each team gets a set of 10 flashcards with key year phrases (e.g., 'I've been to...'). They race to make sentences using the prompts, scoring points for accuracy and speed.
wuAlt: Students do 'Find Someone Who...' with a grid of 8 skills (e.g., 'can write an email') and interview peers to find matches.
Students play 'Vocabulary Pictionary' with 6 target words from the year (e.g., 'interview', 'labour').
pres: Teacher introduces the 'Dream Job Interview' task using a model dialogue on the board. Highlights question forms ('What do you like about...?') and reporting answers ('She said she wanted to...'). Checks understanding with thumbs-up/down for sample questions.
presAlt: Teacher uses a short video of a teen mock interview to elicit target language.
Teacher distributes a 2-sentence handout with question stems and reporting phrases for students to complete.
prac: Students practice in pairs with a 'Job Interview Role Card' (e.g., 'You want to be a video game designer'). They ask 3 questions and report answers using 'He/She told me...'. Teacher monitors and corrects errors.
pracAlt: Students play 'Interview Relay' in teams: one student interviews another, then reports to the group.
Students use a 'Question Bank' handout to match questions to job topics (e.g., 'travel' for pilot).
ls: Students listen to a 2-minute audio of a PET-style interview between two teens discussing their dream jobs. They tick 5 correct statements from a list (e.g., 'Maria wants to be a doctor').
re: After break, students play 'Stand Up, Sit Down' with 5 job-related adjectives (e.g., 'creative'). Teacher calls an adjective, students stand if it describes their dream job.
prod: Students conduct a full 'Dream Job Interview' in pairs (2 minutes each). They prepare 3 questions, interview, then report 2 key answers to the class using 'He/She said...'. Teacher provides a feedback rubric.
rw: Students complete a PET-style reading task: a 150-word text about 'Labour Day in Morocco' with 6 multiple-choice questions. Then, they write a 60-word email to a friend about their Labour Day plans.
st: Teacher shares a short story about a teen's first job experience. Students discuss 1 question: 'What job would you like to try?' Close with: 'You showed your English progress today. Thank you, class!'
g: Teams race to write 5 job-related words from memory.
Students ask a question, next student answers and asks a new one.
Students act out jobs while others guess.
Students bid on correct sentences about jobs.
Teams answer 10 mixed-skill questions for points.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 50-word paragraph about their ideal job interview.
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence starter frame for their interview report (e.g., 'He told me he likes...').
hw: Write your dream-job interview Q&A (6 exchanges).
Review 5 key grammar points from the year (e.g., present perfect).
Complete the PET reading practice handout.
tip: Use Moroccan Labour Day (May 1st) to connect the theme locally—ask students how their families celebrate or what jobs they admire in Oujda.
checklist: I can ask and answer questions about jobs.
I can report what someone said using 'He/She told me...'.
I can understand a 2-minute interview audio.
I can read a short text about Labour Day.
I can write a 60-word email about my plans.
I can use present perfect for experience.
I can use past continuous for descriptions.
